bug_semantics: When createVerifier is configured with a JavaScript RegExp in allowedAud, allowedIss, allowedSub, allowedJti, or allowedNonce, token verification applies that regex via .test() to corresponding JWT claims. Those claims are attacker-controlled once a validly signed token is presented. A catastrophic-backtracking pattern (for example /^(a+)+X$/) plus a crafted claim such as a repeated prefix that fails the terminal atom causes exponential backtracking in the JS regex engine, blocking the Node.js event loop (CWE-1333/CWE-400). String allow-lists are not this bug; the sink is unbounded RegExp.test on attacker-controlled claim values. The library later warns on unsafe regexes but historically performed the match with no complexity or time bound.
flaw_origin: The first implementation of claim allow-list matching in src/verifier.js (ensureStringClaimMatcher plus verifyPayload) accepted objects with a test() method as matchers, including user-supplied RegExp instances, and also compiled string allow-list entries with new RegExp(). It then ran allowed.some(a => a.test(value)) on decoded claims. That first-write established the ReDoS sink: application-supplied regular expressions executed against attacker-controlled JWT claim strings with no safety check. Later commits switched string entries to exact equality (b1d71ed) and wrapped RegExp.test to reset lastIndex (18d2590 / CVE-2026-35040); neither removed unbounded regex matching of claims. GHSA-cjw9-ghj4-fwxf / CVE-2026-35041 remains published (not withdrawn) with affected range >=5.0.0 <=6.2.0; the mechanism itself dates to the 2020 initial verifier.
